title: Heterogeneous index query adaptor and sampled prefetch strategy
creator: Marco Liu
description: Background: Console dashboard query API is experiencing occasional high tail latency for tenant-heavy queries that page deep into time-series results. Existing strategies (time-bucketing + hot-path caching) work for common cases but suffer when tenants have heterogeneous access patterns or when queries hit deep cursor windows. This ticket implements a small query adaptor layer that uses heterogeneous index hints plus a sampled prefetch worker to opportunistically warm multi-tenant caches and reduce tail latency without high memory churn. Goals: reduce p95 for deep pagination queries by at least 30% for top 5% tenants, raise overall cache hit rate for paginated dashboard endpoints, and keep additional memory overhead under 8% per reader shard.
acceptance_criteria: P95 latency on paginated dashboard queries (page >= 3) reduced by at least 30% for top 5% of tenant traffic during synthetic replay
Aggregate cache hit rate for paginated endpoints increases by >= 12% under production-like load
Additional memory overhead per shard is < 8% compared to baseline (measured in canary)
Cursor semantics are preserved (no duplicate or missing rows) in both forward and backward pagination tests
Feature gated with rollout path and ability to fully disable without data migration
technical_notes: Introduce a Query Adaptor layer (middleware between HTTP handler and query planner) that rewrites pagination cursors to add index hints based on tenant profile
Support heterogeneous index hints: time-partitioned primary index, compact per-tenant forward index, and an inverted mini-index for high-cardinality joins
Sampled prefetch worker: per-shard probabilistic sampler that prefetches page N+1 for a small percentage of requests from heavy tenants to warm KV cache and materialized window entries
Adaptive TTLs: cache entries created by sampled prefetch receive short, adaptive TTLs based on subsequent hit rate; hot-lists marked for longer TTLs
Backpressure: prefetch queue size and concurrency are bounded; will fall back to synchronous read if prefetch backlog > threshold
Compatibility: changes implemented entirely at query adaptor/caching layer so underlying storage index formats unchanged
Metric tags: prefetch.{hit,miss,evict,queue_depth} and adaptor.{rewrites,skips,errors} to instrument behavior
rollout_plan: Merge behind feature flag (adaptor.enabled). Default off
Initial canary: enable for 1% of traffic on read replicas for 48h; compare latency and cache metrics to control group
Expand to 10% tenants (tenant sampling by usage tier) for 72h and monitor memory, p95, error rates
If stable, enable for all non-enterprise tenants for 1 week, then enable enterprise tenants with notice
Fallback: feature flag immediate off; fallback path routes to existing query planner and invalidates adaptor-created cache entries
monitoring_and_alerting: Alert: p95_paginated_queries > baseline * 1.5 for 10m after rollout expands
SLO check: no increase in 5xx errors for paginated endpoints after rollout
test_plan: Unit tests for query adaptor rewrite rules and cursor preservation
Integration tests: replay captured production traces with and without adaptor to assert identical result sets
Load test: side-by-side runtime with 10k QPS and synthetic tenant distribution, measure memory and latency
Chaos: simulate slow downstream storage to validate prefetch backpressure and fallback correctness
